clue.text: Pop song in first jam session, as a rule

definitions.text: first jam session, as a rule
definitions.meaning: the White Queen's rule in Through the Looking-Glass is jam tomorrow and jam the day before, but never jam today, so the earlier jam session is the day before today

explanation.surface: Someone explains that a pop song usually comes out of the band's first jam session.
explanation.walkthrough: The White Queen in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass offers 'jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam today', so by her rule the first jam was the day before.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles recorded a much-covered song of this title, and the word also names the day before today.

clue.text: Short call at South Island coming up -this seafarer could make it

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
short means the word for call loses its final letter

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
STH is a standard abbreviation of south
a cay is a small low island or reef

explanation.surface: A brief stop at a southern island is the kind of trip a sailor might manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts NAME to NAM; 'coming up' turns NAM + STH + CAY, giving the answer read upwards. 'at', 'this' and 'could make it' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a pleasure boat is a sailor, a kind of seafarer.

clue.text: Powerful drive succeeded at start of disastrous over

indicators.note: at start of puts the S in front of the following piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: disastrous signals that the letters of over are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: In cricket, a strong shot sets off a disastrous over for the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' is the anagram signal on the cricket word; 'at start of' places the abbreviation first. In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: A servo-mechanism is a power-assisted drive, as in servo brakes or steering.

clue.text: Its even balance between. the sides can produce a solution

definitions.text: Its even balance between. the sides can produce a solution

parts.words: Its even balance between. the sides can produce a solution
parts.note: read as mathematics: something whose two sides are kept equal, and which can be solved to give an answer

explanation.surface: A mediator's even-handedness between two parties can produce a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a peacemaker balancing two sides of a dispute; in fact it is an algebraic statement with an equals sign, solved for its unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical statement that two expressions are equal is balanced across the equals sign and solving it gives a value.

clue.text: Does supply a lot of this material for a tanner

definitions.text: Does supply a lot of this material for a tanner

parts.words: Does supply a lot of this material for a tanner
parts.note: read Does as female animals of the forest, not the verb: the hides they provide are leather for a tanner to work

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a supplier really does provide much of a tannery's material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as the verb 'does supply'; it is the plural of doe, female deer, whose hides a tanner turns into leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide taken from deer, does among them, is leather prepared by tanners.

clue.text: Royal household servant of the old sultanate

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
Oman is an Arabian country ruled by a sultan

explanation.surface: A servant in a royal household once worked for an old sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen of the Guard are ceremonial attendants of the British sovereign, and the word once meant a servant in a noble household.

clue.text: Butterfly, or what's hard on its tail?

definitions.meaning: a European butterfly with a white mark like a punctuation sign on its underwing
a punctuation mark that follows close behind a clause, and has a tail of its own

explanation.surface: A butterfly is pictured, with a question about what is chasing close behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard on' means closely following: this punctuation mark comes right behind the end of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The butterfly is named for the pale curved mark on its wing, shaped like the punctuation sign that separates clauses.

clue.text: Strongbox head of church put up for sale

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word church

parts.note: to offer something is to put it up for sale

explanation.surface: The head of a church puts the parish strongbox up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strong chest for money or valuables.

clue.text: Capuchin' monks, for instance, said it's one way to buy,

indicators.note: said signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the Capuchins are an order of friars, all men, so a male religious order

explanation.surface: Capuchin monks, it is said, do their shopping a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes MALE ORDER (Capuchin monks, a religious order of men) sound like the buying method.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering goods by post from a catalogue is a way of shopping without visiting a shop.

clue.text: He works secretly at collecting information

indicators.note: collecting means the word at gathers the other piece inside itself

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy works covertly at gathering intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' is the container signal: the small word gathers the slang for information inside it. GEN is British slang, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is a spy who works covertly.

clue.text: Drink heavily, having got left out of musical

indicators.note: having got left out of says the letter for left is dropped from the musical's name

parts.note: Carousel is a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical

explanation.surface: Someone hits the bottle after being dropped from the cast of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from CAROUSEL; 'having got' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink freely and noisily in a party.

clue.text: Position in sport that's wrong — or right

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby, being ahead of the ball illegally
the right-hand side of a car or horse in Britain, and in cricket the side a right-handed batsman faces

explanation.surface: A sports position that is wrong, or maybe right.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the off side of a vehicle or horse is the right-hand side, away from the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: The football rule penalises a player in an illegal advanced position, and the off side of a vehicle is its right side.

clue.text: Fish from mouth of Thames to Waterloo

indicators.note: mouth of picks out the opening letter, as a river's mouth is one end

parts.note: a Waterloo is a crushing defeat, as Napoleon's was

explanation.surface: Fish swim from the mouth of the Thames up to Waterloo in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waterloo' looks like the London station on the Thames, but is a decisive defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are freshwater game fish.

clue.text: Drugged, so acted up badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the words before it are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: Being on drugs, someone behaved badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SO ACTED UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced out is slang for dazed, as from drugs.

clue.text: Recalling craft using this device — not needed by Jumbo

definitions.text: Recalling craft using this device — not needed by Jumbo

parts.words: Recalling craft using this device — not needed by Jumbo
parts.note: a memory aid, the trick for remembering things, which an elephant, who never forgets, can do without

explanation.surface: A device for recalling boats is not needed by a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalling craft' suggests calling back boats; it is the art of recall. Jumbo is an elephant, proverbially never forgetting.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme or phrase that helps you remember something is a memory aid.

clue.text: Rag article I tailored badly

indicators.note: tailored badly means the letters are cut and stitched into a different order

explanation.surface: Some clothing, which I tailored poorly, is a rag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I TAILORED. A rag is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article in a newspaper gives the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Change book so woman doesn't get husband in the end

indicators.note: doesn't get says a letter is missing from the woman's name
in the end places the missing letter at the close of the name

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone revises a book so the heroine doesn't end up with a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't get ... in the end' removes the final H from EDITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a book is to revise or alter its text.

clue.text: Time to go round and take child's toy

parts.note: to eddy is to swirl round in circles
to bear is to take or put up with

explanation.surface: It's time to go round and collect a child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed bear is a classic plaything for children.

clue.text: One German moving to Turkish capital, perhaps?

definitions.text: One German moving to Turkish capital, perhaps?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: Turkish capital, read cryptically, is the opening letter of the word Turkish

explanation.surface: A German relocating to Ankara would leave his country behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges I + GERMAN into EMIGRAN; 'capital' adds T. The whole clue also describes someone leaving his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves his own country to settle abroad is an emigrant, as a German relocating to Turkey would be.

clue.text: Soldier's brought in' deranged maniac, a tricky chap to watch

indicators.note: brought in means the soldier is placed within the other letters
deranged says the letters of maniac are disordered

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A soldier has been called in to deal with a mad maniac, a tricky person to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deranged' is the anagram signal on the madman; 'brought in' sets the American soldier inside the rearranged letters. 'tricky chap' points to a conjuror's tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror performs tricks that you have to watch closely to catch.

clue.text: Secure prompt payment 'on this

definitions.meaning: to fasten firmly, as with a metal pin
to pay on the spot is to pay 'on the' this, an idiom for immediate payment

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees that payment will be prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'pay on the nail' means pay at once, said to come from the flat-topped posts (nails) where merchants settled bargains in Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something with a pin is to fasten it; immediate settlement is payment 'on the' spot.

clue.text: One member exposed and weakened

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament
aired means exposed to the open air or brought out publicly

explanation.surface: A politician, once exposed, has been weakened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged or diminished in strength has been impaired.

clue.text: One has no right to fetter a large number of soldiers

indicators.note: has no says a letter is taken out of the fetter

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle for the ankle

explanation.surface: Someone with no right shackles a great many soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' drops R from LEG IRON; 'One' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion was a large body of troops, and the word also means a vast multitude.

clue.text: Military bar, that gets charges down

definitions.meaning: a stiff metal rod, emblem of rigid soldierly bearing
the rod used to force powder and shot down a muzzle-loading gun barrel

explanation.surface: A military bar, perhaps a canteen, that cuts its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like prices; it means gunpowder charges rammed down a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod for ramming a charge into a muzzle-loader was standard soldiers' kit.

clue.text: Shock-wave noise resounded behind English missile

indicators.note: behind places the word for resounded after the letter for English

parts.note: a boom is the loud noise of a shock wave, as a sonic boom
a bell that rang has resounded

explanation.surface: A shock wave's noise rang out behind an English missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick that returns to the thrower is an Aboriginal Australian missile.

clue.text: British tripe with hot soup

parts.note: tripe and rot both mean nonsense
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: British tripe served with hot soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like the offal dish; it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a thin soup made from stock.

clue.text: I agree one of the lines must go, though trains ran on time here

definitions.text: though trains ran on time here

indicators.note: must go says one letter is dropped from the word for agree

parts.note: accounts that tally agree
L is the abbreviation for line, and the word for agree contains two of them

explanation.surface: Someone agrees a railway line must close, though the trains did run to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini was famously said to have made the trains run on time in this country. 'must go' removes one L from TALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascist Italy under Mussolini was proverbially the place where the trains were punctual.

clue.text: This can tease out some fraud, I trust

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An investigation might uncover some fraud, one hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts can uncover fraud.

clue.text: Actor, one appearing in more demanding title role in musical

indicators.note: appearing in means the numeral is placed inside the name of the role

parts.words: more demanding title role in musical
parts.note: Oliver Twist famously asks for more in the musical Oliver!
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An actor appears in the demanding lead role of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more demanding' looks like 'more difficult'; it means asking for more, as Oliver does.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film actor.

clue.text: Operatic heroine's song before death is over

indicators.note: before places the song in front of the next piece

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: is over says the word for death is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: the end of life is death

explanation.surface: An opera heroine sings her final song before her death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns END to DNE. Strauss wrote Ariadne auf Naxos.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne is the title role of Strauss's opera Ariadne auf Naxos.

clue.text: Queen whose appearance saved 1000 bottles of champagne?

definitions.text: Queen whose appearance saved 1000 bottles of champagne?

parts.words: Queen whose appearance saved 1000 bottles of champagne?
parts.note: Marlowe's face that launched a thousand ships: ships were launched with that face, so no bottle needed breaking

explanation.surface: A queen's arrival spared a thousand bottles of champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships are launched by smashing champagne on the bow; Marlowe called the queen of Sparta's face the one that 'launched a thousand ships', saving the bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of Sparta whose abduction caused the Trojan War had a face that launched a thousand ships.

clue.text: One 'sets off to bring back list of duties observed

indicators.note: bring back says the whole string of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
noted means observed

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to fetch back a list of duties he noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring back' reverses ROTA + NOTED as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that triggers an explosion is what sets off a bomb.
